newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares tumble, puzzled brokers blame liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares tumble, puzzled brokers blame liquidity.

text.p: Greek equities started the week in a bearish mood and traded in negative territory with selling pressure more pronounced in construction and small-caps. The market closed off session lows, down 1.03 percent with many brokers puzzled by the fall.

"I cannot explain Monday's fall. We came through the elections with a strong four-year government and the market should be cruising higher. It must be a chronic illness of liquidity. Major domestic players are overbought and the market needs new money," said broker Giuseppe Gianno at Euroxx Securities.

"We could go down to 940 and then attempt a mild rebound. Foreign players have not injected serious cash at this juncture and there is also a wait-and-see attitude as players await concrete moves by the government on economic policy," he said.
The finance ministry's end-September T-bill issue went on sale on Monday featuring three-, six- and 12-month T-bills at unchanged rates of 11.90, 12.10 and 12.70 percent respectively.

Greece's new socialist cabinet was sworn in last week with Yannos Papandoniou elevated to economic "czar", heading both the national economy and finance ministries. The socialists have a comfortable 162-seat majority in the 300-seat parliament.
Prime minister Costas Simitis is meeting with his cabinet's top economic ministers on Monday evening to discuss action on the economy and the 1997 budget.
The Athens general share index closed 1.03 percent, or 9.94 points lower at 953.61, off the session's low of 950.44 from Friday's 963.55 close after opening at 964.82 points.
Turnover slipped to 7.58 billion drachmas on volume of 3.98 million shares.

Decliners led gainers 166 to 42 with 27 issues unchanged on 235 traded. Banks lost 0.79 percent, industrials fell 1.07 percent and construction tumbled 1.89 percent. Small-caps settled with sharp losses of 2.56 percent.
